How this book matches your board exam. Research check: this book follows NCERT Class 10 History, India and the Contemporary World – II, Chapter 1 (The Rise of Nationalism in Europe), for the CBSE 2026–27 session. The Social Science theory paper is 80 marks in 3 hours, plus 20 marks of internal assessment. History, Geography, Political Science and Economics carry 20 marks each. The paper uses 1-mark MCQs (including assertion–reason), 2-mark short answers, 3-mark answers, 5-mark long answers, 4-mark case/source-based questions and map work. The two board exams continue: Phase 1 is compulsory, and Phase 2 is optional for improving marks.

Each unit ends with a 10-mark practice set built from these question types. The marking points are our own, not the official CBSE marking scheme. Check the latest sample paper on cbseacademic.nic.in before your exam.

Unit 1 of 10: Sorrieu's Vision and the Idea of the Nation

Key ideas

  • In 1848, the French artist Frédéric Sorrieu made four prints showing his dream of a world of democratic and social republics.
  • The first print shows people of Europe and America marching past the Statue of Liberty, holding a torch of Enlightenment and the Charter of the Rights of Man. On the ground lie the shattered symbols of absolutist rule.
  • Peoples are grouped as nations, identified by their flags and national costumes. Christ, saints and angels look on from heaven — a symbol of fraternity among nations.
  • Absolutism: unrestricted, despotic, authoritarian rule by a monarch. Utopian: an ideal society that is unlikely to exist.
  • Nation-state: a state in which most citizens, not just rulers, develop a sense of common identity and shared history.

Worked examples

Example 1 (2 marks): "What is a utopian vision?" → A vision of a society so ideal it is unlikely ever to exist (1); Sorrieu's world of democratic republics is one such vision (1).

Example 2: In Sorrieu's print, the USA and Switzerland lead the procession because they were already nation-states by then.

10-mark practice set

  1. (1 mark, MCQ) Frédéric Sorrieu's prints (1848) showed a dream of: (a) a world of empires (b) democratic and social republics (c) a European monarchy (d) a world government under the Pope. Answer: (b).
  2. (1 mark) What is absolutism? Answer: a system of unrestricted, despotic rule by a monarch.
  3. (3 marks) Describe three features of Sorrieu's first print. Answer: peoples march past the Statue of Liberty (1); shattered symbols of absolutism in the foreground (1); nations shown by flags and costumes, with Christ and angels above symbolising fraternity (1).
  4. (5 marks) What is a nation-state? How did the idea differ from the older dynastic empires of Europe? Answer: citizens share a common identity and history (1); people, not just rulers, feel belonging (1); old empires were ruled by dynasties over many peoples (1); loyalty was to the ruler, not the nation (1); nationalism made the nation the source of political power (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Dating Sorrieu's prints wrongly (1848). 2. Confusing "utopian" with "real". 3. Vague description of the print. 4. Defining nation-state as "a country with a king". 5. Missing the fraternity symbolism.

Quick recall

  1. Who made the 1848 prints? 2. Which nations lead the procession? 3. Define utopian. 4. What lies shattered in the foreground? 5. What symbolises fraternity?

Answers: 1) Frédéric Sorrieu. 2) USA and Switzerland. 3) An ideal but unlikely society. 4) Symbols of absolutism. 5) Christ, saints and angels above.
